groups.title: Prisma Schema Design
groups.question: You are designing the database for a Next.js app with users, posts and tags using Prisma, and the schema will change as features grow. Explain how you would model and evolve it.

followUps.Defining models, fields, and scalar type: How does a Prisma model map to the database?
followUps.Relations: one-to-many and many-to-many: How would you model posts with one author and many tags?
followUps.Migrations workflow and schema evolution: How do migrations keep everyone's database in sync?

evidence.text: The Prisma schema is the single source of truth for the database structure.
Models map to tables and fields to columns.
Scalar types like String and DateTime map to database column types.
A one-to-many relation stores a foreign key on the many side.
Relation fields let you navigate from either model.
Many-to-many uses a join table that Prisma can manage for you.
migrate dev writes SQL migrations from schema changes and applies them.
Migration files are committed and applied in order everywhere.
Changes that move or reshape data need extra steps to avoid losing it.

notEnough: Only saying migrations update the schema.

groups.title: Query Patterns
groups.question: Your post list must be filtered, sorted and paged, and creating a post with tags must never leave half-saved data. Explain how you would write these queries.

followUps.Filtering, sorting, and pagination with: Why is cursor pagination better than offset for large lists?
followUps.Nested writes and transactional operatio: How do nested writes and transactions keep related records consistent?

evidence.text: Prisma queries take typed where, orderBy, take and skip options.
Skipping many rows gets slower as pages get deeper.
Cursor pagination continues from the last item and stays fast.
Nested writes create or connect related records in one query.
$transaction runs several operations so they all succeed or all fail.
This prevents half-finished data if one step fails.

groups.title: Prisma Setup and Tooling
groups.question: A new developer needs a working local database with realistic data. Explain how you would set up Prisma, inspect data and seed it.

followUps.Install Prisma and configure database co: What do you need to connect Prisma to a local PostgreSQL?
followUps.Prisma Studio for visual database inspec: What is Prisma Studio useful for?
followUps.Seeding the database with realistic test: How do you seed the database and make it safe to rerun?

evidence.text: Install the Prisma CLI and the Prisma client.
Set DATABASE_URL in an environment file.
Running PostgreSQL in Docker gives every developer the same database.
Prisma Studio is a browser interface for the database.
You can browse and edit records.
It quickly confirms that migrations and writes did what you expected.

notEnough: Only saying it is a GUI.

evidence.text: A seed script creates consistent starting data.
It is registered so prisma db seed runs it.
Using upserts makes it safe to run repeatedly.

groups.title: Prisma in Next.js
groups.question: In development your app starts throwing 'too many connections' errors after a few code changes. Explain why and how you use Prisma safely in Next.js.

Why does hot reloading exhaust database connections, and how does a singleton fix it?
followUps.Type-safe CRUD with generated Prisma typ: What do generated Prisma types give you in practice?

evidence.text: Hot reloading re-runs modules and can create a new Prisma client each time.
Each client opens its own connection pool, so connections run out.
Storing one client on the global object reuses it across reloads.

notEnough: Only saying you use a singleton.

evidence.text: Prisma generates TypeScript types from the schema.
Every query result is typed, including selected fields and relations.
Typos and wrong field types are caught before the code runs.
